proposals: PPAC should publish an official Petrochemical Intensity Index for every Indian refinery each year, with a stated definition of which streams count, so the national 13% and company targets can be checked against one methodology rather than press reports of investor calls.

IOCL should state its group-wide PII target, and the refinery-wise path to it, in its annual report, so the 15% versus 16% discrepancy between its earnings-call transcript and press coverage is settled in a primary filing.

PPAC should split naphtha production and imports by grade — petrochemical-grade versus fuel use — in its Ready Reckoner, so the constraint it already flags, that domestic naphtha is often unsuitable for chemical use, can be measured as new refinery capacity comes on stream.

The Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals should publish a product-wise table matching planned cracker and polymer capacity at Panipat, Paradip, Barmer, Andhra Pradesh and Nagapattinam against imports of products such as LDPE/LLDPE and PET, so the claim that rising PII will substitute imports can be tested.

IOCL and CPCL should publish the final configuration, capacity and revised cost of the Nagapattinam project once the review concludes, so the shift from a 9 MMTPA refinery to a petrochemical complex is recorded in a primary document rather than trade press.
